verdict.rationale: TypeSafe documents a dedicated LLM-guardrails cookbook. It screens every message going into and out of an LLM app and thresholds hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route. A confidence-routing pattern explicitly gates whether to act, and a citation-check cookbook catches hallucinated output. This satisfies the 'documented patterns for gating model output' branch of the story. missing for 10: a dedicated moderation endpoint or built-in safety settings (gating is built from generic Choice/Score/Noul questions), in-depth evidence of the hazard taxonomy beyond the cookbook summary, independent or hands-on corroboration of guardrail use, and robustness against adversarial content, which the vendor itself lists as a known jagged edge.

support.subject: As a developer, the platform gives me guardrail primitives — moderation endpoints, safety settings, or documented patterns for gating model output before it acts

citations.quote: Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.
The answer tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act.
Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document.
